short: Recognising that one's own awareness is Shiva — liberation as re-cognition rather than new attainment.
beginner: Pratyabhijna means recognition, like suddenly recognising a friend you had forgotten. Kashmir Shaivism says liberation is recognising that you already are Shiva — nothing new has to be made.
what: Pratyabhijna is both a key idea and the name of a philosophical school within non-dual Kashmir Shaivism. It holds that the individual is Shiva, the universal consciousness, which has freely concealed itself by limiting its own powers; liberation is the recognition of this identity. Unlike Advaita's changeless Brahman, the Shiva of Pratyabhijna is dynamic and self-aware, and the world is a real expression of that consciousness rather than an illusion.
scholar: The school was founded by Somananda (Shivadrishti) and systematised by Utpaladeva (Ishvara-pratyabhijna-karika) and Abhinavagupta, who wrote two commentaries on it. Kshemaraja's Pratyabhijna Hridayam is a concise primer. Central technical terms are prakasha (light of consciousness) and vimarsha (its reflexive self-awareness); the malas (limitations) and the thirty-six tattvas explain how Shiva appears as limited beings. The school argued extensively against Buddhist logicians.

perspectives.view: The self is Shiva; bondage is self-forgetting through Shiva's own power of concealment, and liberation is recognition, which can be sudden through grace or gradual through practice.

Advaita shares the non-dual identity of self and absolute but treats the world as an appearance (vivarta) of changeless Brahman, whereas Pratyabhijna treats the world as the real self-expression of dynamic consciousness.

The Pratyabhijna philosophers developed their position largely in debate with Buddhist logicians who denied a lasting self; the Buddhist side held that memory and recognition can be explained without one.

follow.note: Its opening teaching identifies the self with consciousness.
